title: Lord Crane
translation: Lord Crane was called Master Crane as a boy. People who say he got the name because he kept cranes have it wrong.
original: {田鶴|たづ}の{大殿|おほいどの}は、{童名|わらはな}たづ{君|ぎみ}なり。
「{鶴|つる}を{飼|か}ひ{給|たま}ひける{故|ゆゑ}に。」と{申|まう}すは{僻事|ひがごと}なり。
literal: The Tazu no Ōidono's childhood name was Tazu-gimi.
Saying 'It is because he kept cranes' is a mistake.

notes.text: The 1925 edition identifies him as Kujō Motoie, a son of the regent Kujō Yoshitsune. {田鶴|たづ}: an old word for 'crane', used mostly in poetry. {大殿|おほいどの}: a respectful title for a senior noble, often a minister or the father of a regent.
{童名|わらはな}: the name a boy of good family used before his coming-of-age ceremony, when he received an adult name. {君|ぎみ}: 'young lord'.
{僻事|ひがごと}: 'a mistake, something wrong'. Kenkō corrects a popular explanation, briefly and without discussion.
